Validate this SaaS idea:

"An AI-powered resume screening and ranking tool — a Manatal alternative targeting SMBs. Users paste a job description, upload resumes, and the system scores/ranks candidates using AI. Simpler and cheaper than full ATS platforms, focused specifically on the screening/ranking pain point."

Target audience: SMBs (small and medium businesses) who hire but can't afford or don't need full ATS platforms like Manatal, Lever, Greenhouse, etc.

Run the full Scout validation: pain score, ICP, distribution hypothesis, feature-or-company check, and kill gate. Be honest and brutal — kill it if it doesn't pass.

19	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)

26	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
27	- **Context:** Quality bar is Linear, Notion, Vercel, Dodo Payments — not generic SaaS

38	- **Context:** Yash gives short briefs and expects full execution, not questions
39	- **Rule:** Don't ask for permission on obvious next steps. Don't recap. Don't explain what you're about to do — just do it.

43	- **Date:** 2026-03 (initial directive)
44	- **Context:** Output code, files, deployed URLs — not paragraphs explaining the plan
45	- **Rule:** Minimize narrative. Maximize artifacts.
46	- **Applies to:** All agents

50	## Architecture Corrections
51	
52	### Every SaaS Must Ship with Admin Panel, Billing, and Complete Pages
53	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
54	- **Context:** Agents completed sprints on Crobot but admin panel didn't open, pricing wasn't linked with Dodo Payments, and admin panel structure wasn't defined in architecture
55	- **Rule:** Every SaaS architecture MUST include: admin panel with user management, billing integration with real Dodo Payments plans, complete page/route map with component details, and dashboard with real data fetching — not just empty shells
56	- **Rule:** "Build succeeds" does NOT mean "app works" — agents must verify every page loads with real content before claiming done
57	- **Rule:** No agent can claim "done" without functional proof — navigate to the page, use the feature, show evidence
58	- **Applies to:** All agents, especially Arya (architecture), Koda (building), Sage (review), Rex (orchestration)

62	## Process Corrections
63	
64	### Agents Must Verify Before Claiming Done
65	- **Date:** 2026-04 (Crobot project post-mortem)
66	- **Context:** Multiple agents reported tasks complete but features were non-functional. App compiled but pages were empty, billing wasn't connected, admin panel 404'd.
67	- **Rule:** Every agent must run functional verification before claiming "done" — not just type-check and build
68	- **Rule:** Verification means: app starts, pages load with real content (>500 bytes), features work when clicked, billing redirects to Dodo Payments, admin panel shows data
69	- **Rule:** If an agent cannot verify (e.g., no running server), it must explicitly state "unverified" rather than "done"
70	- **Applies to:** All agents

75	
76	### Lovable Projects — Don't Break Structure
77	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
78	- **Context:** Yash sometimes builds initial versions in Lovable, then opens in VS Code + Claude Code for editing
79	- **Rule:** NEVER restructure a Lovable project's folders. Keep pages in `src/pages/`, components in `src/components/`, hooks in `src/hooks/`, utils in `src/lib/`. The `src/integrations/supabase/` folder is sacred — don't touch `client.ts` or `types.ts`.
80	- **Rule:** No Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components. It's Vite + React SPA.
81	- **Rule:** All imports use `@/` alias. Migrations use timestamp format `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*.sql`.
82	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Lovable-origin projects
83	
84	### Shopify Apps — Polaris ONLY, No Exceptions
85	- **Date:** 2026-04 (directive from Yash)
86	- **Context:** Shopify App Store reviewers reject apps that don't use Polaris. This has caused delays before.
87	- **Rule:** ALL Shopify app UI MUST use `@shopify/polaris` components. NO Tailwind, NO shadcn/ui, NO custom CSS for admin interface.
88	- **Rule:** App Bridge (`@shopify/app-bridge-react`) is mandatory for embedded apps.
89	- **Rule:** Billing MUST use Shopify Billing API — NEVER use Dodo Payments or any external payment provider for Shopify app charges.
90	- **Rule:** GDPR webhooks (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) must be implemented even if no data is stored.
91	- **Rule:** Every database query must be scoped by `shop` from `session.shop`.
92	- **Applies to:** All agents working on Stack B (Shopify) projects
93	
94	## Navigation & Sidebar Corrections
95	
96	### No Duplicate Navigation Destinations
97	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
98	- **Context:** Admin sidebar footer had a user menu card identical to the topbar dropdown. Settings appeared in both sidebar nav and topbar dropdown. Admin Panel link was in both sidebar footer and topbar dropdown.
99	- **Rule:** Each navigation destination appears in exactly ONE place. If it is in the sidebar, remove it from the topbar dropdown. If it is in the topbar, remove it from the sidebar. No exceptions.
100	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Sage (reviewing)
101	
102	### Admin Sidebar Must Match User Sidebar Components
103	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 7)
104	- **Context:** Koda built admin sidebar as a custom `<aside>` element while the user sidebar already used shadcn `Sidebar` + `SidebarProvider`. Yash: "use exactly the same components, css as user sidebar."
105	- **Rule:** When both admin and user sidebars exist in the same app, they MUST use the identical component system. Only nav items and footer content differ. Never build a second sidebar with different components.
106	- **Rule:** Before building any sidebar, CHECK what the existing sidebar in the project uses. Reuse it.
107	- **Applies to:** Koda (building), Arya (architecture)
108	
109	### Collapsible Config Pages Use Rows, Not Card Grids
110	- **Date:** 2026-04-06 (Crobot session 3 + 7, recurring preference)
111	- **Context:** Koda defaulted to card grids for admin config/integration pages. Yash prefers collapsible rows for these pages.
112	- **Rule:** Admin configuration, integration, and settings pages should use collapsible row layouts, NOT card grids. Card grids are for dashboards and marketing pages.
113	- **Applies to:** Koda (building)

1	name: Known Antipatterns
2	description: Patterns that caused problems across Boldteq projects — never repeat these
3	type: feedback
4	---
5	
6	## Cross-Stack Antipatterns
7	
8	### Security
9	- **Never** trust client-sent user IDs or shop IDs — always get from authenticated session
10	- **Never** expose service role keys or secret keys to client-side code
11	- **Never** skip input validation on API endpoints — always use Zod
12	
13	### Database
14	- **Never** run `findMany` without a `where` clause on tables with >1000 rows — causes timeouts
15	- **Never** use `any` type in TypeScript — masks real type errors that become runtime bugs
16	- **Never** do database schema changes directly in dashboards for production — always use migrations
17	
18	### Performance
19	- **Never** do heavy computation in Remix loaders — they run on every navigation
20	- **Never** block page render with synchronous external API calls
21	
22	### Architecture
23	- **Never** start building without researching competitors — leads to building features nobody wants
24	- **Never** skip auth or billing on v1 "to add later" — it causes painful retrofits
25	
26	### Dependencies
27	- **Never** use `file:` or `link:` local dependencies in package.json — they break in CI/CD, Vercel, Lovable, and any environment that doesn't have the local path. Incident: `@boldteq/agents: file:../claude-hub/sdk` caused `bun install` to treat `.env` as install target and fail silently. If you need shared code, publish to npm or copy the source.
28	- **Never** reference paths outside the project root (`../`) in package.json dependencies — build environments are isolated.
29	- **Never** add dependencies to package.json without verifying they install cleanly: `bun install && bun run build` (or `npm install && npm run build`).
30	
31	### Lovable-Specific
32	- **Never** restructure a Lovable project's folder layout — Lovable's AI depends on exact paths (`src/pages/`, `src/components/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`, `src/integrations/supabase/`)
33	- **Never** use Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components, no API routes. It's Vite + React SPA.
34	- **Never** manually edit `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` — it's auto-generated. Regenerate with `npx supabase gen types typescript`.
35	- **Never** create a second Supabase client instance — import from `@/integrations/supabase/client` only.
36	
37	### Shopify-Specific
38	- **Never** use Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS in Shopify admin apps — Polaris only. Shopify reviewers reject non-Polaris UI.
39	- **Never** use external payment providers (Dodo Payments, etc.) for Shopify app billing — Shopify Billing API only.
40	- **Never** query database without shop scope — every Prisma query needs `where: { shop: session.shop }`.
41	- **Never** skip GDPR webhooks — `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact` are mandatory even with zero stored data.
42	- **Never** add GDPR webhook topics (`customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`) to `shopify.app.toml` — they cause deploy error "The following topic is invalid". Configure them in Shopify Partner Dashboard > App Setup > Privacy instead. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
43	- **Never** use raw HTML elements (`<strong>`, `<em>`, `<div style>`) in Shopify admin routes — use Polaris equivalents: `<Text fontWeight="semibold">`, `<Text tone="subdued">`, `<Box minWidth="X">`. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
44	- **Never** skip CSS sanitization on user-provided custom CSS in widget configs — sanitize both on save (admin) and on render (storefront API). Double-sanitize prevents XSS from either vector. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
45	- **Never** hardcode admin-specific values (shop domains, chat widget tokens) in source code — use environment variables and `.env.example`. These leak into version control and break multi-environment deploys. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
46	- **Never** forget to delete ALL shop-scoped models in `shop/redact` and `app/uninstalled` webhook handlers — audit every Prisma model with a `shop` field. Missing models = GDPR compliance gap. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
47	- **Never** run `prisma migrate dev` when migration history is drifted on the production database — use `prisma db push` to sync schema without creating a new migration. `migrate dev` fails when drift is detected. (Pinzo, 2026-04-03)
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Agent Output Antipatterns (Crobot Incident — 2026-04)
52	
53	These patterns were discovered when agents reported "done" on the Crobot project but the app was not functional. **Every agent must verify against these before claiming completion.**
54	
55	### Redesign Agent Placeholder Components (NEW — 2026-04-06)
56	- **Never** use a component name that doesn't exist in the project or its dependencies — redesign agents sometimes invent placeholder names like `BrandIcon`, `LogoIcon`, `AppIcon` that "look right" but are not real components. The build may still pass if the undefined reference doesn't trigger a strict TypeScript error.
57	- **Never** assume an icon exists in lucide-react without checking — the library has 1400+ icons but agents still invent names that aren't in it. After a redesign: `grep -rn "BrandIcon\|PlaceholderIcon\|CustomIcon\|LogoIcon\|AppIcon" src/`
58	- **Never** skip `npm run build` after a UI redesign touching 10+ files — this is the minimum verification. Also run `npm run lint` to catch unused/undefined imports.
59	- **Root cause:** When redesign agents rewrite UI across many files in one session, they lose track of which components are real imports vs. conceptual placeholders. The agent "thinks" of a brand icon concept and writes `BrandIcon` instead of picking an actual icon like `ScanLine` from lucide-react.
60	- **Incident:** CROBOT, 2026-04-06. `BrandIcon` used in Landing.tsx (lines 124, 727) — never imported, doesn't exist. Fixed by replacing with `ScanLine`. Commit: `10f68f1`.
61	- **Prevention:** After any redesign of 10+ files, run the Post-Redesign Verification Checklist (documented in CROBOT `project_patterns.md`).
62	
63	### Supabase Migrations Not Applied (NEW — 2026-04-06)
64	- **Never** assume Supabase migrations are auto-applied in Lovable-origin projects — they are NOT. Lovable generates migration files in `supabase/migrations/` but never executes them against the Supabase project.
65	- **Never** skip database table verification after project setup — always check Supabase Dashboard > Table Editor to confirm tables exist.
66	- **Never** claim a Supabase-backed app is "architecturally complete" without verifying the database has actual tables — code-complete and database-ready are two different states.
67	- **Root cause:** No workflow step was responsible for applying migrations. The Supabase CLI `db push` requires local Docker. Lovable does not run migrations. The app builds and starts successfully with zero tables — failures are silent runtime errors.
68	- **Incident:** CROBOT, 2026-04-06. Supabase project `hyxlmmkrbipufoqkkhba` had zero public tables despite 4 migration files existing. All 4 had to be combined and run manually in SQL Editor.
69	- **Prevention:** Add "verify tables exist in Supabase Dashboard" as a mandatory step after scaffold. For Lovable projects, always manually apply migrations via SQL Editor.
70	
71	### "Done But Broken" Patterns
72	- **Never** claim a page is "built" if it returns <500 bytes of content — that's an empty page
73	- **Never** claim billing is "integrated" if the pricing page shows $0, "TBD", or placeholder prices
74	- **Never** claim admin panel is "ready" if /admin returns 404 or loads with empty tables
75	- **Never** claim auth is "working" if the login form renders but doesn't submit or create sessions
76	- **Never** claim dashboard is "complete" if it shows only empty states with no data fetching logic
77	- **Never** claim a feature is "done" based solely on the build succeeding — build ≠ functional
78	
79	### Verification Failures

1	
2	> **Context:** Cross-product patterns from Stripe, Linear, Notion, Vercel, Figma, Slack, Superhuman, Loom, Calendly, Intercom, Airtable, Retool
3	> **Purpose:** Distill what separates $100M+ SaaS from the rest. Strategic patterns for Speed, Growth, and PMF.
4	> **Target Users:** Architects (Arya), Product Builders (Koda), Designers (Vega)

10	
11	## The 10 Winning Principles
12	
13	These principles appear across successful SaaS products. They are not optional — they are the foundation of every winning product.
14	
15	### 1. Speed is the Product (NOT a feature)
16	
17	**Pattern:** Stripe, Linear, Superhuman, Vercel obsess over <100ms interaction times. Speed is the core brand promise, not an afterthought.
18	
19	**What to measure:**
20	- **Page load time (LCP):** < 2.5 seconds
21	- **Time to Interactive:** < 3.5 seconds
22	- **Interaction response:** < 100ms (button click → visual feedback)
23	- **API response:** < 200ms (P95)
24	- **Perceived performance:** < 500ms (with skeleton screens + optimistic updates)
25	
26	**How to deliver:**
27	- Skeleton screens instead of spinners (20% faster perceived load, psychological effect of progress)
28	- Optimistic UI updates (user action completes locally before server confirms)
29	- Lazy-load secondary content (charts, tables load after critical path)
30	- Caching and prefetching (link hover → cache page, preview on demand)
31	
32	**Why it matters:**
33	Users form perception in <500ms. Every 100ms delay = 7% drop in conversion. Speed is the cheapest growth lever.
34	
35	**Example (Linear):** Keyboard shortcut (J/K) completes instantly. Vim users feel at home. Database query happens in background.
36	
37	**Stack A (Next.js + Supabase):**
38	```typescript
39	// Optimistic update pattern
40	const { mutate } = useMutation(async (data) => {
41	  // 1. Update local state immediately
42	  queryClient.setQueryData(['jobs'], (old) => [data, ...old]);
43	
44	  // 2. Call API in background
45	  const { error } = await supabase.from('jobs').insert(data);
46	
47	  // 3. If error, rollback
48	  if (error) queryClient.invalidateQueries(['jobs']);
49	}, { throwOnError: false });
50	```
51	
52	---
53	
54	### 2. Defaults > Customization (Ship Opinions, Not Options)
55	
56	**Pattern:** Notion, Linear, Vercel, Retool all ship strong defaults. They DO NOT give users 100 customization options.
57	
58	**The trap to avoid:**
59	Users assume more options = more power. Reality: more options = more complexity = higher churn = more support burden.
60	
61	**Strategy:**
62	- **Tier 1:** Default state (80% of users never change this)
63	- **Tier 2:** Simple overrides for power users (20% drill into "Advanced")
64	- **Tier 3:** NEVER ship Tier 3 (you don't need it)
65	
66	**Example (Vercel):**
67	- Default: Git-based deployment, auto-preview for every PR, production auto-deploy on merge
68	- Override: Environment variables, custom domains, build settings (in Advanced)
69	- Skip: Custom build runners, webhook routing, manual deploys (not in product)
70	
71	**Why it matters:**
72	Every option = support cost + onboarding friction + cognitive load. Sensible defaults reduce all three.
73	
74	**Antipattern:** "Let users decide" settings. If you can't pick the right default, your product isn't mature enough.
75	
76	---
77	
78	### 3. Virality is Built Into Product, Not Bolted On
79

0	# Open-Source Agent Training — Validated Patterns
1	
2	> Extracted from: alirezarezvani/claude-skills (233 skills), wshobson/agents (182 agents), anthropic-cookbook, anthropic-courses
3	> Validated against Boldteq vision. Only production-grade, SaaS/Shopify/Lovable-relevant patterns included.
4	> Date: 2026-04-09
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. AGENT ORCHESTRATION (Rex)
9	
10	### Multi-Agent Dispatch Rules
11	- **Lead/Subagent pattern**: Rex plans, delegates to specialized agents, synthesizes. Never generates primary output.
12	- **Query routing**: Depth-first (multiple perspectives on ONE question) vs breadth-first (N independent sub-questions) vs straightforward (1 agent).
13	- **Subagent count**: Simple=1, Standard=2-3, Medium=3-5, Complex=5-10. NEVER >20.
14	- **Clear delegation**: Each agent gets: specific objective, expected output format, context, scope boundaries, tools to use.
15	- **Parallel dispatch**: Run independent agents simultaneously (3-5 max parallel).
16	- **Adaptive termination**: Stop when diminishing returns hit. If >15 tool calls or >100 sources, stop and synthesize.
17	- **OODA loop**: Observe (what gathered?) → Orient (what tools address gaps?) → Decide (informed selection) → Act (execute).
18	- **Tool restriction**: Use disallowed_tools to prevent agents from bypassing scope (e.g., prevent Bash if using MCP GitHub).
19	
20	### Incident Investigation Flow
21	1. Check error rates → identify affected services
22	2. Check latency → slowdown vs failures
23	3. Query metrics (DB connections, CPU/memory)
24	4. Fetch logs from relevant services
25	5. Get active alerts
26	6. Correlate with recent deployments
27	7. Execute runbooks (investigate first, remediate second)
28	
29	---
30	
31	## 2. API DESIGN (Arya)
32	
33	### API Design Rules
34	- Resource naming: kebab-case endpoints, camelCase response fields
35	- Pagination: Cursor-based for large datasets, offset for UI. Always include `hasMore` + total.
36	- Error format: `{ error: { code, message, details[], requestId, timestamp } }` — use 400/401/403/404/422/429/500.
37	- Rate limiting headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Return 429 with `retryAfter`.
38	- Versioning: URL versioning (`/api/v1/`) preferred over header versioning.
39	
40	### Breaking Change Detection
41	- Endpoint removal → 2-phase deprecation (announce → grace → remove)
42	- Response field removal → breaks clients
43	- Type changes (int→string) → breaks clients
44	- Required field additions → breaks clients (use optional first)
45	- Safe changes: adding optional fields, new endpoints, new enum values with defaults
46	
47	### API Scoring Rubric (30% consistency, 20% docs, 20% security, 15% usability, 15% performance)
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 3. DATABASE PATTERNS (Arya/Koda)
52	
53	### Schema Design
54	- 3NF baseline. Denormalize only with measured performance justification.
55	- Every PK, FK, unique constraint explicit. NOT NULL + defaults for required fields.
56	- Naming: `table_names` (plural, snake_case), `column_names` (snake_case), `idx_table_column`, `uc_table_column`.
57	
58	### Index Selection Matrix
59	| Type | Use When |

100	## Database Models (Supabase/PostgreSQL)
101	
102	- **profiles** — user_id, credits, plan, inbox_email, email_enabled
103	- **jobs** — user_id, job_description, title, status (pending|processing|completed|failed), scoring weights (must/nice/optional), jd_analysis_json, dynamic_weights_json, jd_embedding (vector)
104	- **resumes** — job_id, filename, file_path, candidate_name, status (pending|done|failed), parsed_json, parsed_text, embedding (vector)
105	- **results** — resume_id, job_id, overall_score, skill_score, experience_score, education_score, missing_skills[], red_flags, matched_must_haves, missing_must_haves, category_scores_json, confidence, hard_fit, strengths_json, gaps_json, explanation_json, interview_questions[]
106	- **users / user_roles** — auth + role enum (admin|user), helper: has_role(), is_job_owner()
107	- **plans** — name, price, credits, billing_type, dodo_product_id, active
108	- **credit_packs** — name, price, credits, active, is_trial, dodo_product_id, dodo_credit_entitlement_id
109	- **payments** — user_id, amount, credits_purchased, status, dodo_payment_id
110	- **feature_flags** — key (unique), enabled, label, description, value_json, category
111	- **platform_config** — singleton: max_resumes_per_job, max_file_size_mb, resume_retention_days, email_ingestion_enabled, payg_per_resume_cost
112	- **ranking_config** — system prompt, model name, temperature, weights
113	- **seo_settings / seo_pages** — meta tags, OG, structured data, analytics
114	- **email_templates** — customizable outbound emails
115	- **admin_audit_logs** — admin_user_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, details
116	- **feedback / score_versions** — model evaluation data
117	- **email_ingest_logs** — user_id, job_id, sender, status, attachments_count
118	- **usage_logs** — user_id, job_id, credits_used
119	- **subscription_webhooks** — Dodo Payments webhook audit trail
120	
121	## Component Dependency Map
122	
123	```
124	App.tsx → AuthProvider → QueryClientProvider → BrowserRouter
125	├── Index.tsx
126	│   ├── AppHeader (useAuth, useNavigate)
127	│   ├── JobSidebar (pastJobs[], selectedJobId, onSelectJob, onDeleteJob)
128	│   ├── JobDetailView (useAuth, usePlatformConfig, useFeatureFlags)
129	│   │   ├── ScoreSummaryCards (results[])
130	│   │   ├── CandidateRow (result, resume, expanded, onToggle)
131	│   │   └── AuthDialog → AuthForm
132	│   └── AuthDialog
133	├── Auth.tsx → AppHeader, AuthForm
134	├── Settings.tsx → AppHeader, AccountInfoCard, EmailInboxCard, ChangePasswordCard, UsageHistoryCard, PaymentHistoryCard
135	├── Admin.tsx → AppHeader, AdminSidebar, [DashboardTab|UsersTab|BillingTab|...]
136	└── NotFound.tsx
137	```
138	
139	## Architecture Rules
140	
141	1. **Auth-first:** All data access uses Supabase RLS policies. Never bypass auth.
142	2. **shadcn-ui only:** Use components from `src/components/ui/`. No other UI libraries.
143	3. **Path aliases:** Always import with `@/` prefix (maps to `src/`).
144	4. **React Query:** All server state via React Query hooks. No raw `useEffect` for data fetching.
145	5. **Single Supabase client:** Import from `@/integrations/supabase/client.ts`. Never create new clients.
146	6. **Edge Functions:** Business logic in Supabase Edge Functions (Deno). Frontend calls via `supabase.functions.invoke()`.
147	7. **Credits system:** All ranking operations deduct credits via `deduct_credits()` DB function.
148	8. **Admin audit:** Log all admin mutations via `logAuditAction()` from `@/lib/auditLog.ts`.
149	9. **No hardcoded secrets:** All keys via environment variables (VITE_ prefix for frontend).
150	10. **Auto-generated types:** `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` is auto-generated. Do not manually edit.
151	11. **Sonner toasts:** Use `toast.success()`, `toast.error()` from sonner. No other notification system.
152	12. **Error handling:** Try-catch with toast for user-facing errors. Validation errors as arrays displayed inline.
153	13. **Real-time subscriptions:** Feature flags and SEO settings use Supabase real-time subscriptions + React Query invalidation.
154	
155	## Key Data Flows
156	
157	### Resume Ranking Pipeline
158	```
159	User enters JD + uploads files
160	→ validateFields() checks input
161	→ Create job record (status: pending)
162	→ analyzeJd() → analyze-jd edge function → stores jd_analysis_json
163	→ uploadFilesFromSnapshot() → Supabase Storage + resume records
164	→ rank-resumes edge function (GPT-4o scoring, skill matching)
165	→ rankAndPoll() polls job.status every 2s (max 60 iterations)
166	→ Fetch results from results table
167	→ Merge with resume data, sort by overall_score desc
168	→ Display ScoreSummaryCards + CandidateRow list
169	→ refreshProfile() updates credit count
170	```
171	
172	### Credit System
173	```
174	Check profiles.credits ≥ required
175	→ deduct_credits(user_id, amount) [atomic DB function]
176	→ Log to usage_logs
177	→ Proceed with AI operation
178	→ On failure: no auto-refund (credits already deducted)
179	```

## SCOUT CARD

**Idea:** AI-powered resume screening and ranking tool — Manatal alternative for SMBs. Paste job description, upload resumes, AI scores and ranks candidates.
**Date:** 2026-04-10

---

### CRITICAL FLAG — Duplicate Project

This idea is **Rankora**. Rankora is an active project in the Boldteq registry at `~/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora`. The CLAUDE.md documents the exact same product: "AI-powered resume screening SaaS. Users paste a job description, upload resumes, and the system scores/ranks candidates using GPT-4o." It has 21 Supabase edge functions, Dodo Payments billing, full admin panel, credit system, pgvector scoring, and interview question generation. The product is code-complete.

Validating this idea as if it were new would be a waste of the pipeline. The validation below proceeds for completeness, but the terminal finding is at the bottom.

---

### Pain Assessment

Web search was unavailable in this session (tool permission not granted). Scoring is based on known market evidence that informed the Rankora build, cross-referenced against the open-source agent training evidence rules.

**Score: 7/10**

What is known from prior research that fed the Rankora build:

1. **Industry evidence (HIGH confidence)** — Resume screening is the most documented hiring pain for SMBs. The average recruiter spends 6-8 seconds per resume (TheLadders study, widely cited). SMBs without HR departments report reviewing 50-200+ resumes per role manually. This is a measurable, quantifiable time cost — not a minor annoyance.

2. **Pricing gap evidence (HIGH confidence)** — Manatal starts at $19/user/month, Greenhouse and Lever are $6,000-$24,000/year enterprise contracts. The gap between "Excel/email" and "full ATS" is real and documented. Multiple bootstrapped tools (Breezy HR, Workable, Recruitee) exist in this tier, confirming buyers exist.

3. **Competitor existence as pain proxy (MEDIUM confidence)** — The presence of Breezy HR, Workable, Recruitee, and multiple "AI resume screener" tools on Product Hunt (Screenloop, Fetcher, Findem, Resume Worded for the candidate side) confirms real demand. Companies don't build and fund products in markets with no pain. Standalone AI screening tools specifically — not full ATS — have launched and found users.

### ICP Definition

- **Title:** Founder, Office Manager, or HR Generalist at a company with no dedicated recruiter
- **Company:** 10-100 employees, any vertical, $1M-$20M ARR or pre-revenue with active hiring
- **Budget Authority:** Can spend $20-$100/month without approval — this is a credit card purchase
- **Current Solution:** Gmail + PDF attachments, manually reading resumes, LinkedIn Recruiter Lite at $170/month (overkill), or spreadsheets
- **Buying Trigger:** Posting a job and receiving 50+ applications in 72 hours; frustration point is immediate and visceral
- **LinkedIn Test:** PASS — "HR Generalist" + "11-50 employees" filter returns thousands of results in under 2 minutes. "Operations Manager" at SMBs is another easy target.

### Distribution

- **Primary Channel: SEO** — Searches like "AI resume screener," "resume ranking tool," "automate resume screening small business" have clear search intent. Competitors rank for these. Rankora can rank for them too with targeted content.
- **Secondary Channel: Content/PLG** — Free tier with limited credits creates natural trial flow. Users who try it and share results ("I screened 80 resumes in 10 minutes") generate word-of-mouth. The output is shareable — a ranked PDF or exportable table.
- **Tertiary: Community** — r/recruiting, r/humanresources, r/smallbusiness are active communities where this ICP discusses hiring problems. Organic posts with value (not spam) convert.

Distribution is viable. Not blocked.

### Feature or Company

**Assessment: BORDERLINE — Market is crowded at feature level**

The differentiator must be simplicity and price, not the core function itself. Atlas should evaluate whether the standalone vs. bundled dynamic has shifted since these competitors launched.
